copy.headline: Most people use their freezer for ice cream, frozen pizza, and meat.
items: It can hold almost everything in your kitchen —
if you freeze it at the right time.

copy.headline: Bread.
items: Slice before freezing — pull individual slices straight to the toaster. No thawing needed.
This alone saves most households $3–5/week in stale bread waste.

copy.headline: Cheese.
items: Hard and semi-hard cheeses (cheddar, mozzarella, parmesan) freeze for 6+ months.
Shred before freezing — frozen blocks crumble when thawed. Shredded cheese goes straight from freezer to pan.

copy.headline: Cooked rice and grains.
copy.body: Cool completely. Freeze flat in bags. Reheat with a splash of water. Lasts 4–6 months. Frozen rice actually makes BETTER fried rice than fresh — the texture is dryer and crisps up faster.

copy.headline: Fresh herbs.
items: Drop a cube into any pan and you have instant herb butter. One tray lasts 2 months.

copy.headline: The rule: Freeze food BEFORE it expires, not after.
items: Freezing doesn't fix food that's already gone bad. It suspends food that's still good.
Time the freeze, and you never throw that item away again.

copy.headline: Your freezer is the most underused appliance in your kitchen.
copy.ctaLine: fond tells you the ideal freeze date for every item — so you pause time instead of wasting it. Link in bio.
